clue.text: Dismal measure once given backing in newspaper

indicators.note: in places the turned measure inside the name of the newspaper

parts.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper

indicators.note: given backing means the old measure is written from right to left

parts.note: the ell is an obsolete measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A gloomy old measurement reported backwards in a tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sullen is sulky and gloomy, so the word is a synonym of dismal in mood.

clue.text: Girl needs to avoid appearing ignorant

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
ware is an old verb meaning beware of or avoid, as in 'ware hounds'

explanation.surface: A girl must take care not to look uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of something means having no knowledge of it.

clue.text: Sluggishness of monkey taking nothing in

indicators.note: taking with in means the monkey takes the next letter into itself
in completes taking in, placing the zero inside the monkey's name

parts.note: the langur is an Asian monkey
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lazy monkey that takes nothing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is listless inertia, a state of lethargy.

clue.text: American money can ultimately purchase all needs

parts.note: can and nick are both slang for prison

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Dollars and cents can buy everything we need in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickels are US five-cent coins.

clue.text: Facades presented by experts on the crest of a wave?

indicators.note: in an across clue the experts come on, that is after, the surf

parts.note: surf is the foaming crest of breaking waves
aces are experts or top performers

explanation.surface: Experts riding the crest of a wave present a fine show to onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Facades are outward faces or exteriors, which is what surfaces are.

clue.text: Garments submerged in northern river

parts.note: under means beneath the water, submerged
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Clothes go under in a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The WEAR flows through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is clothing worn beneath outer garments.

clue.text: Fussy female — one engaged in criminal activity

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nicking is British slang for stealing

explanation.surface: A woman who is particular about details turns to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Finicking means excessively fastidious or particular.

clue.text: Genevan clubs with an inclination to limit French wine

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to limit means the lean holds the French wine in its bounds

parts.note: a list is a tilt or lean
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A Swiss card player inclined to ration his wine.
explanation.walkthrough: John Calvin led the Reformation from Geneva, so a Genevan in religion is his follower.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin's Geneva was the centre of his Reformed faith, so a Calvinist is a Genevan by creed.

clue.text: Old Poet Laureate bagging game in wind

indicators.note: bagging means the poet's name captures the game inside, as a hunter bags quarry

parts.note: Robert Southey was Poet Laureate from 1813 to 1843
RL is rugby league

explanation.surface: A former Laureate shoots game on a windy day.
explanation.definitionFit: A southerly is a wind blowing from the south.

clue.text: Peer drops ring where country dance is held

indicators.note: drops means the ring-shaped letter is let fall out of the nobleman's title

parts.note: a baron is a peer of the realm
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A nobleman loses his ring at a rustic dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A barn dance is a country dance traditionally held in a farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: Barn dances are named for the farm building in which such dances were held.

clue.text: Coloured in confusion about mark, particularly in top class

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for note well
in confusion says the letters of the colour word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means mark well or note particularly

explanation.surface: A muddled note about colouring in, from someone at the top of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' turns COLOURED into CORDOLEU, which goes 'about' NB.
explanation.definitionFit: The French blue ribbon denotes the highest class, especially of cooks.

clue.text: Mellow old city in China

indicators.note: in places the ancient city inside the word for a friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate = mate)
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city in China ripens gently.
explanation.walkthrough: China is a capital here to mislead: it is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellow and mature both describe something ripened or softened by age.

clue.text: Mistake about joint being slightly salty

indicators.note: about means the word for an error goes around the cut of meat

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
a rack is a joint of meat, as in rack of lamb

explanation.surface: A cook's error over a joint makes it taste a bit salty.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water has a mild saltiness, as in estuaries where sea meets river.

clue.text: Females endlessly grabbing attention is so annoying

indicators.note: grabbing means the shortened word for females holds the next pieces inside
endlessly means the final letter of the word for females is cut

parts.note: women are females
to give ear is to give attention

explanation.surface: Women who keep demanding attention are a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims WOMEN to WOME, which is 'grabbing' EAR and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome is tiresome, tedious and irritating.

clue.text: Magazine reported by artist for harassment of dissenters

indicators.note: reported means the magazine title is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Which? is a British consumer magazine
William Holman Hunt was a Pre-Raphaelite painter

explanation.surface: A painter is reported in a magazine for persecuting critics.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch-hunt is a campaign persecuting those holding unpopular views.

clue.text: One's left Mediterranean port in one of the Queens

indicators.note: left means the letter for one has gone from the port's name

parts.note: Alexandria is an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean
I is one, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: Someone has sailed from an Egyptian port to visit a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Alexandra was the consort of Edward VII.

clue.text: Get from printer pretty piece to read

indicators.note: get from says the letters are extracted from the following words
piece means only a run of letters inside the words is taken

explanation.surface: Fetch a nice extract from the printer to study.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret a text or sign is to read its meaning.

clue.text: Preoccupation of pupil once with academic terms

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
a session is an academic year or term

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy fixated on his university terms.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation that dominates the mind.

clue.text: Here, in France, the monarch is more hostile

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: In France, the king or queen is in a frostier mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means colder, and a cold manner is an unfriendly one.

clue.text: From time to time, interrupted by little bird's cry

indicators.note: interrupted by means the two time letters have the small word put between them

parts.note: wee is Scots and informal for little

explanation.surface: Every so often a small bird breaks in with its call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From time to time' reads as T to T, a pair of Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is the chirp of a small bird.

clue.text: Brisk private secretary brought back, with good reason

indicators.note: brought back means the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for private secretary
rightly means justifiably, with good reason

explanation.surface: An energetic secretary was rehired, and justly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy, as brisk does.

clue.text: Hun, possibly, driven out, having taken area

indicators.note: out says the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Attila's warriors were driven out after taking territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huns were invaders of the Roman Empire, so a Hun is an example.

clue.text: Fish I save to sustain little boy

indicators.note: in a down clue, to sustain means the following pieces sit beneath the boy

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry
but means save, except

explanation.surface: I rescue a fish to feed a small boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish.

clue.text: Escaping charge for disclosure of secrets

definitions.meaning: electric current seeping away through faulty insulation

explanation.definitionFit: Leakage means both a slow escape of electricity and unauthorised release of information.

clue.text: Crown's support a doctor needed in changing these

indicators.note: changing says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor is needed to change these royal supports.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown is the top of the head, not a monarch's crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest supports the top of the head, which is the crown.

clue.text: Like some fraction of the populus?

definitions.meaning: describing a common fraction such as three-quarters, with numerator over denominator
populus is Latin for the people, so this means belonging to the common people

explanation.walkthrough: A vulgar fraction is a common one; Latin vulgus, like populus, means the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar, from Latin vulgus, means common, both of fractions and of ordinary folk.

clue.text: Fur carried by a French theologian gradually wore out

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: carried by means the fur is held within the French article and divinity degree

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian
ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: A French theologian in an ermine gown slowly wore himself out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Doctor of Divinity is the convention for a theologian; the fur sits between the two letters of that degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine is to weaken or erode gradually, as by digging beneath.

clue.text: Problems are commonly experienced in this same craft

definitions.text: Problems are commonly experienced in this same craft

parts.words: Problems are commonly experienced in this same craft
parts.note: the idiom of all being in the same vessel means sharing a common difficulty, and craft is a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: To be in the same boat is to share a predicament; a boat is a craft.

clue.text: Browning's way of honouring absent friends

definitions.meaning: making bread go brown before a fire or grill
raising glasses to drink to people not present

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Browning's manner of remembering friends far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasting means both browning bread and drinking to someone's health.

clue.text: Bishop suppresses articles? I'll say!

indicators.note: suppresses means the bishop's abbreviation sits on top of the articles, holding them inside

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A bishop censors some newspaper pieces, and emphatically so.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather! is a hearty British exclamation of agreement, like Certainly!
